problems.description: frontmatter.ts hand-rolls a YAML parser (parseSimpleYaml/parseScalar/parseValue) and merges it over gray-matter's output, even though gray-matter natively parses YAML — the inline rationale ('gray-matter only understands JSON frontmatter here') is factually wrong. This is a second divergent parsing path for the same input that drives the measured cognitive complexity (+35) and will need reconciling as later sessions extend frontmatter.

The seed codebase (root index.ts — a Minimal Express Todo API, a mismatched seed for the SSG story) was left untouched and unremoved. It is now orphaned dead code excluded from tsconfig (rootDir: src) that also collides conceptually with the new src/index.ts barrel; the +4671/-0 line count shows nothing was cleaned up.

Missing-content-dir error handling relies on an uncaught throw propagating out of the commander action (non-zero exit, but no structured error/exit-code handling); CLI tests spawn ts-node subprocesses with 20s timeouts, which is slow and somewhat fragile for exit-code coverage.
renderMarkdown casts marked.parse(...) to string with { async: false } to mask the string|Promise union — the likely source of the measured +1 SonarQube bug signal.

Measured convention score 0.60 with 81 violations, but the sampled violations reference files not in this commit (dev-server-plugin.ts, markdown-plugin.ts — added in session 4). The lint measurement appears repo-wide rather than commit-scoped, over-attributing later-session debt; this commit's own code is largely compliant (PascalCase interfaces, camelCase functions, const/let only, JSDoc).

strengths: Faithful to the session-1 spec: commander CLI with --content/--output, marked, gray-matter, jest, strict TypeScript, per-page HTML + index.html into ./dist
Clean layered module decomposition (cli → build → frontmatter/markdown/templates/types) that maps directly onto the architecture of the later sessions (templates, dev server, plugins)
18/18 jest tests passing across 4 suites (frontmatter, markdown, build, CLI) with proper tmp-dir setup/teardown, and an end-to-end build verified during the session
No artifacts committed (node_modules/dist/dist-bin gitignored), separate tsconfig.build.json excludes tests, clean focused commit
commit_reviews.summary: A faithful, fully-tested greenfield SSG foundation with clean module layering, slightly dragged down by a redundant hand-rolled YAML parser and an orphaned mismatched seed file left in the tree (measured convention 0.60 is repo-wide and over-attributes later-session violations).

problems.description: getTemplateEngine(templatesDir) is constructed once per buildPage call (inside the pages.map) plus again for the index render — the engine could be created once and shared across all page renders.

SonarQube reports +14 cognitive complexity and +2.8% duplication; the FALLBACK_LAYOUT string replicates the HTML structure the refactor was meant to consolidate, which is the likely duplication source.

The CLI now defaults --templates to ./templates but no templates/ directory ships with the repo; whether absence of that directory silently falls back to FALLBACK_LAYOUT or errors is not verifiable from this diff and should be explicit.

strengths: Replaces hand-rolled HTML string interpolation with a real templating engine, reducing the maintenance surface while preserving escaping semantics (Handlebars auto-escapes title/date; {{{body}}} is intentionally raw for markdown output).
Well-scoped abstraction: templatesDir threads cleanly through cli.ts → build() → buildPage(), with a defaultTemplatesDir() helper matching the existing codebase style.
Pinned handlebars ^4.7.9, a patched release that resolves the prototype-pollution CVEs in earlier versions — safer than the manual escapeHtml it replaces.
SonarQube delta of +0 bugs / +0 smells; the new `template` field on Page and frontmatter-driven per-page template selection extend the existing data flow without breaking it.
commit_reviews.summary: A coherent feature addition that replaces fragile string-built templates with a proper Handlebars engine threaded cleanly through the CLI and build pipeline; note the 0.60 convention score is repo-baseline noise — all 81 listed violations are in index.ts/dev-server-plugin.ts/markdown-plugin.ts, files untouched by this commit — so this diff itself introduces no new convention violations.

problems.description: 81 convention violations (convention score 0.60) across index.ts, dev-server-plugin.ts, and markdown-plugin.ts — non-PascalCase class/interface names, use of 'var', and non-UPPER_CASE constants, per the mechanical scan.
+29 cognitive complexity concentrated in the dev-server integration; the watch+websocket wiring lands a large amount of control flow in a single session (+482/-10 lines, +9 functions).
No test files accompany the new watch/websocket functionality (AST diff adds 2 source files only); websocket broadcast and file-watch retry logic are exactly the paths that need coverage.

chokidar and ws are idiomatic choices for a live-reload dev server, but chokidar pulls ~12 transitive deps (anymatch, braces, glob-parent, readdirp, ...) into the runtime dependency graph for what is a dev-only feature.

strengths: New functionality is isolated in a plugin (dev-server-plugin.ts) that slots into the existing plugin architecture alongside markdown-plugin.ts.
Dependency selection is idiomatic and correct for the task: chokidar for file watching, ws for websocket live reload, @types/ws scoped to devDependencies.
No new bugs introduced and duplication improved by 0.8%.
The commit delivers its session goal (integration) as a self-contained, reviewable change.
commit_reviews.summary: Adds a chokidar+ws dev-server plugin that fits the SSG's plugin architecture and session intent, but lands with a 0.60 convention score (81 violations) and +29 cognitive complexity, trading maintainability debt for the integration milestone.

problems.description: dev-server-plugin couples to the owning engine via the injected rebuild callback while also owning its own watcher; rebuild orchestration is split between engine and plugin, so live-reload silently breaks if rebuild isn't wired. The broadcast-then-rebuild timing is implicit.

Plugin pipeline order is implicit: markdown-plugin sets page.body and template-plugin consumes it, yet the Plugin interface carries no ordering metadata — a future plugin inserted between them would silently corrupt the pipeline.

dev-server-plugin onEnd closes the WebSocketServer and only then terminates clients after the close callback fires — clients are terminated after the server has already stopped accepting; the order should be reversed.
Inconsistent null-handling of ctx.outputDir: template-plugin guards with `if (!ctx.outputDir) return` while dev-server-plugin casts `ctx.outputDir as string`.

Measurement reports 81 convention violations (score 0.60), including 'Use const or let instead of var' and 'Constants should be UPPER_CASE' nits; most listed items are 'Classes/Interfaces should use PascalCase' flags on factory-returned object types, which appear to be analyzer false positives.
package.json bin/main now point at dist-bin/src/* — this must match the build output layout; no guard ensures the paths stay in sync with tsconfig.build.json outDir.

strengths: Reuses existing modules (renderMarkdown, getTemplateEngine) rather than reimplementing; no new bugs or smells, duplication reduced -0.5%.
commit_reviews.summary: Sound plugin refactor that respects the existing Plugin interface and reduces duplication, with minor coupling (dev-server rebuild callback), implicit plugin ordering, and shutdown-ordering wrinkles — though the measured 0.60 convention score appears inflated by analyzer false positives on factory-returned object types, the code reads cleaner than the raw score suggests.

compounding_issues: Vestigial seed file: the root index.ts (an Express Todo API, unrelated to the SSG story) was left untouched and committed through all 5 sessions — dead, unreferenced code (excluded from tsconfig's rootDir:src build) that no session cleaned up.

Hand-rolled flat-YAML frontmatter parser merged over gray-matter (documented as supporting only scalars/arrays, no nested maps) became a latent constraint every later session had to interoperate with rather than fixing it once.
Compiled dist-bin/*.js artifacts were regenerated into the working tree in sessions 3 and 5 (gitignored, not committed) — housekeeping noise in the agent's own files_created lists.

The Handlebars choice in Session 2 rippled forward: Session 4's template-plugin and Session 5's template-hash invalidation both had to special-case .hbs layouts/partials, coupling cache correctness to the template directory layout.
key_decisions: Session 4's plugin-system refactor (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd lifecycle hooks, engine.ts + config.ts) — the pivotal architecture; it turned the Session 3 dev server into a plugin and directly enabled Session 5's incremental builds to thread through the pipeline.
Deliberately split lifecycle: async onStart/onEnd vs synchronous build hooks, keeping the public build API synchronous and letting the dev server reuse one engine instance across rebuild passes.

Incremental-cache design: versioned .ssg-cache.json manifest keyed by source-hash + resolved-template-hash + combined-partials-hash, with graceful fallback to clean build and a rolling avgPageBuildMs time-saved estimate.
Strict-mode TypeScript with a separate tsconfig.build.json (rootDir:src → gitignored dist-bin) and a src/index.ts barrel export — a clean public API surface maintained across all sessions.
Pragmatic frontmatter handling: a hand-rolled simple-YAML parser merged over gray-matter output rather than adding a YAML dependency.
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality was high and stable across all five sessions, with a slight upward arc. Session 1 established a tested, strict-mode TS core (build/cli/frontmatter/templates + 4 test files) under the early_degrade perturbation (4 retries, confidence 0.86), and every subsequent session landed on top of it: Session 2 added a real Handlebars layout/partial system with tests (confidence 0.93), Session 3 integrated a live-reload dev server with watch-and-rebuild, Session 4 executed the riskiest and most expensive step (62K tokens, $2.61) — a clean plugin extraction that shrank serve.ts from ~166 to a thin wrapper while updating tests — and Session 5 capped the arc with a genuinely non-trivial cross-cutting feature (hash-based incremental builds with a versioned cache manifest) that correctly reuses the Session 4 engine hooks. Declining per-session confidence (0.93 → 0.80) tracks growing complexity rather than degradation, and test_executed_success=true with all_successful=true confirm the code stayed green throughout.
story_review.summary: A textbook five-session arc — core → feature → integration → refactor → cross-cutting — where the Session 4 plugin architecture was the load-bearing decision that let Session 5's incremental build land cleanly, marred only by a never-removed vestigial seed file.
